title: The youngest guide
text:
At just nineteen, Oskar Wójcik is one of the youngest licensed tour guides in Kraków. He shows tourists around the city in four languages. We met him in a café in the Main Square.

How did you become a guide?
I've always loved history. When I was fourteen, I started reading everything about Kraków, and I used to give "tours" to my family when relatives visited. Last year I passed the official exam. It was really hard – there were questions about every church and every king!

Which languages do you speak?
Polish, of course, English, German and Spanish. My mother is from Spain, so Spanish was easy. I learned German at school and from watching TV series. English I practise every day with tourists.

Do tourists trust such a young guide?
At first some of them are surprised. Once an older American man asked me if my father was the real guide! But after ten minutes, when they see how much I know, they relax. I think my age is actually an advantage: I talk to people in a natural way and I'm not boring.

What is the most difficult part of the job?
The weather and the questions! In winter it's freezing, and you're outside for three hours. And tourists sometimes ask questions you can't prepare for – once someone asked me how many pigeons live in the Main Square.

What are your plans for the future?
I've just started studying history at university. I'd like to write a guidebook about the hidden places in Kraków – the small streets and courtyards that tourists usually miss. Maybe one day I'll make videos about them, too.
